title: Reasons for Reforms: Debido a and A Raíz de

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the formal cause connectors *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6, and *porque* from A1. They give the reason or starting point of an event and take a noun. The reforms of Batlle and the Constitution of 1917 are good places to use them: each event led to the next.

sections.title: Reason + result
rows: Debido a la ley de 1915, los obreros trabajaban ocho horas al día.
A raíz de la reforma de 1877, la escuela pública es gratuita y obligatoria.
*a raíz de* + noun: as a result of
Debido a la Constitución de 1917, la Iglesia y el Estado quedaron separados.
La escuela pública es laica porque la ley lo establece.

items.spanish: Debido a la ley de 1915, los obreros trabajaban ocho horas al día.
items.english: Because of the law of 1915, workers worked eight hours a day.

items.spanish: A raíz de la reforma de 1877, la escuela pública es gratuita y obligatoria.
items.english: As a result of the reform of 1877, public school is free and compulsory.

items.spanish: Debido a la Constitución de 1917, la Iglesia y el Estado quedaron separados.
items.english: Because of the Constitution of 1917, Church and State were separated.

items.spanish: La escuela pública es laica porque la ley lo establece.
items.english: Public school is secular because the law says so.

sections.content: After *debido a* and *a raíz de* put a noun, never a verb: *debido a la ley*, not *debido a se aprobó la ley*. With a masculine noun, *a* + *el* becomes *al*: *debido al divorcio*. Use *porque* before a verb.
